proposed_changes.before: Active as of 2026-09-23; in effect through February 17, 2027 unless ended sooner. The City is defending a lawsuit filed in Dakota County District Court by Eagan Capital (owner/operator of an existing Eagan data center) around late June/early July 2026, after the City denied Eagan Capital a temporary use permit in May 2026; Eagan Capital seeks to void the moratorium. No ruling had been reported as of 2026-09-23.
proposed_changes.after: Recorded active; present legal force remains unverified. MPR News reported on July 7, 2026 that Eagan Capital filed its moratorium challenge on June 15, seeking $50,000 and disputing the city’s authority over electricity demand. CBS Minnesota reported on November 9 that the city was separately suing the company over chiller permits, zoning and noise allegations; it reported that the mayor announced the legal action on November 2. These are reported claims and actions, not judicial findings. Case identifiers, court orders, subsequent moratorium amendments and actual project applicability remain unverified.

proposed_changes.before: Pending study and possible permanent regulations
proposed_changes.after: A moratorium challenge and a separate city enforcement action have been reported. Court dispositions and any resulting change to the moratorium’s operative force remain unverified.

facts.value: MPR reported that a complaint on behalf of Eagan Capital was filed on June 15, 2026, challenging Eagan’s data center moratorium.
facts.supporting_summary: The July 7 report identifies the company, the city and the reported filing date.

facts.value: MPR reported that Eagan adopted a one-year moratorium on new or expanded data centers in February 2026.
facts.supporting_summary: The report describes the duration and adoption month of the city’s pause.

facts.value: MPR described the moratorium as focused on development projects using more than 20 megawatts within 500 feet of homes.
facts.supporting_summary: This is the newsroom’s description, not authenticated ordinance text.

facts.value: Eagan Capital alleged that the city lacked authority to impose the suspension and sought $50,000 in damages. Its attorneys argued that the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission has exclusive authority over electricity demand.
facts.supporting_summary: MPR attributes these claims to the complaint and the company’s attorneys; it does not report a judicial finding.

facts.value: CREdocket reported that the company’s suit was filed in Dakota County District Court and sought relief striking down the moratorium.
facts.supporting_summary: The derivative index provides these details, but the supplied material contains no authenticated complaint or docket verifying them.

facts.value: Eagan told MPR that it denied an interim use permit after staff identified temporary trailer-mounted chillers installed and operating without required permits. The city said the proposed use was unlawful under the property’s zoning.
facts.supporting_summary: These are the city’s stated reasons for the permit denial, not court findings.

facts.value: Eagan said it intended to defend the moratorium through the legal process.
facts.supporting_summary: MPR reported the city’s stated litigation position.

facts.value: CBS Minnesota reported that Eagan sued Eagan Capital, alleging that temporary chillers were operating without proper permits.
facts.supporting_summary: The reported city enforcement action concerns the chillers and is distinct from the company’s earlier moratorium challenge.

facts.value: Mayor Mike Maguire announced the city’s legal action at a November 2, 2026, council meeting.
facts.supporting_summary: CBS identifies an announcement date, not the date the city’s suit was filed.

facts.value: CBS reported that a company representative told the council in May that the company did not believe a permit was needed for the chillers, applied after being notified, and designed a sound barrier.
facts.locator: Paragraph about the May council representation
facts.supporting_summary: The account is attributed to the company representative.

facts.value: CBS reported that the city also denied a mechanical permit application for permanent chillers and alleged that noise exceeded code despite the sound barrier.
facts.supporting_summary: The report attributes the zoning rationale and noise allegation to the city’s lawsuit.

facts.value: MPR’s report is dated July 7, 2026, with a July 8 correction. CBS’s report is dated November 9, 2026, at 10:45 p.m. CST, which is November 10 UTC. CREdocket repeats the MPR reporting and is not independent corroboration.
facts.supporting_summary: The supplied source roles and article timestamps distinguish the reports and their relationship.

uncertainties: No authenticated complaint, ordinance, order or official docket was supplied; reported legal language and the exact moratorium scope are not independently verified.
The filing date of the city’s chiller enforcement suit is not established by the November 2 announcement.
The supplied reports do not establish a ruling, injunction, the moratorium’s legality, or whether it remained in force later.
Dates attached to CREdocket’s related stories concern other matters, not events in the Eagan cases.
No candidate or current row was supplied for comparison.
